newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-10 pct of assets underperforming-BHP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-10 pct of assets underperforming-BHP.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Monday that about 10 percent of the company's assets were underperforming, based on the company's 10 percent return on capital investment criteria.
"They've got to improve or they've got to go," managing director John Prescott told reporters.
Prescott did not specify which assets were under-performing.
He said assets would be looked at within the context of the company's operating divisions.

For example, Prescott said, the TEMCO manganese smelter at Bell Bay in Tasmania was under-performing although within the context of the company's manganese division it would have to be looked at differently.
Prescott said on Friday that TEMCO (Tasmanian Electro Metallurgical Co) did not meet the company's hurdle rates in terms of earnings but that the manganese business as a whole did.

Last Friday, BHP announced a 1996/97 (June-May) net profit of A$410 million, 60.8 percent lower than the year-ago level after abnormal writedowns of A$976 million, with more than half from the copper division led by Magma in the United States.
There were writedowns also in the other three divisions -- steel petroleum, and minerals.
BHP shares were 24 cents higher at A$19.39 at 11.35 a.m. (0135 GMT) on Monday.
